gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-gruppo: Gruppo reads crisp, its curve endings keeping well apart. Happy Monkey is best loud and large, its marker-nib line ignoring direction, while Gruppo does its best work in quiet, tidy text.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-gudea: Gudea reads friendly and modern, with gaps clear as glass. Over page after page its thread-thin curves stay easy on the eye, while Happy Monkey's ruler-straight strokes sit loudly above.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-hanken-grotesk: Lines look wire-bent across each word, with wide channels leading into every counter. Hanken Grotesk is built for steady reading, whereas Happy Monkey is built to grab attention with ruler-straight strokes.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-host-grotesk: Host Grotesk is a contemporary sans-serif whose curves sweep open rather than curling shut. And Happy Monkey earns its keep big and brief, where one unchanging stroke width gives each letter a bold stamp.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-ibm-plex-sans-ara: Easily readable open apertures give the text a clean, approachable face beside Happy Monkey's wire-thick, bold strokes. IBM Plex Sans Arabic can be sized down quite far before those apertures start to crowd.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-ibm-plex-sans-dev: Modern and loose, the body's rope-like curves never knot at the ends. Happy Monkey does its best work as a bold, measured-stroke headline, while IBM Plex Sans Devanagari does its best as quiet running text.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-ibm-plex-sans-heb: Bent-straw letters up top, friendly ones below: Happy Monkey leads and IBM Plex Sans Hebrew follows. And its open, uncrowded mouths on the s and c let the sans text flow smoothly across a full page.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-ibm-plex-sans-jp: Steady, unvarying lines up top, clean open curve endings below: Happy Monkey and IBM Plex Sans JP make an easygoing, sturdy duo. One is best at shouting, the other at carrying sentences.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-ibm-plex-sans-kr: IBM Plex Sans KR stays open at every curve end, modern and uncluttered. IBM Plex Sans KR slots in beneath Happy Monkey, whose strokes never swell where curves meet stems, so the two sit comfortably.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-ibm-plex-sans-tha: IBM Plex Sans Thai reads modern, its c ends pointing apart like open pincers. Happy Monkey's w, with no thick or thin strokes, gives the heading a bold stamp, and the body lets it speak.
